Metadata.description: A free, privacy-first training dashboard for triathletes. Your training, finally clear.

hero.title: Your training, finally clear.
hero.subtitle: Connect Garmin or Strava and see your swim, bike, run and strength training the way it should be shown. Free, and only for your eyes.

features.title: Everything that matters, on one screen

weekly.title: Weekly overview
weekly.text: Training hours split by swim, bike, run and strength, compared week by week.

averages.title: Your typical week
averages.text: Average volume per sport over any period, from 4 weeks to all time.

bestEfforts.title: Best efforts
bestEfforts.text: Your fastest 5 km, 10 km, half and full marathon, bike records and best power.

goals.title: Goals
goals.text: Set a target like 5 km in 15:00 and see how far you are and what to work on.

countdowns.title: Race countdowns
countdowns.text: Your next race, always one glance away.

activities.title: Activity log
activities.text: Every session from Garmin and Strava, grouped by week.

privacy.title: Your data stays yours
privacy.onlyYou: Only you can see your data. No feeds, no leaderboards, no public profiles.
privacy.noAds: No ads, no data selling and no AI training on your data.
privacy.control: Export or permanently delete everything at any time.

Footer.disclaimer: Stramin is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Garmin or Strava.

Guide.title: Import your Garmin history
Guide.intro: Garmin only sends new activities to Stramin. To see your full history, download a copy of your data from Garmin once and upload it to Stramin.

open.title: Open your Garmin account
open.text: Log in to your Garmin account and go to data management.

request.title: Request your data
request.text: Click "Export Your Data" and then "Request Data Export".

wait.title: Wait for the email
wait.text: Garmin sends you an email with a download link. It usually takes about 48 hours, but can take up to 30 days.

download.title: Download the file
download.text: Open the link in the email and download the ZIP file. Don't unzip it.

upload.title: Upload it to Stramin
upload.text: Upload the whole ZIP file to Stramin. Coming soon.

Guide.note: You only need to do this once. After that, new activities arrive automatically through the Garmin connection.

signup.title: Sign up
signup.consent: By signing up you accept our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

forgot.title: Reset password
forgot.intro: Enter your email and we will send you a link to choose a new password.

success.checkEmail: Almost there! Check your email and click the link to confirm your account.
success.resetSent: If an account exists for that email, we have sent a link to reset your password.

connect.title: Connect your training data
connect.text: Connect Strava to see your full training history. Garmin users can also import their history with a one-time download.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.stravaNotConnected: Connect Strava to estimate your best efforts from your activities.

bestEfforts.title: Best efforts
bestEfforts.note: Strava values are estimates from your activities' average pace: exact for races, a bit slow when your fastest effort was inside a longer workout. Tap ✎ to enter your real time.
bestEfforts.unavailable: Your own values can't be saved yet: the database needs an update first.

level.title: Your running level
level.explain: VDOT is a running fitness score from Jack Daniels' Running Formula. Your training paces follow from it.
level.noRuns: Add a running best effort to see your level and training paces.

Training.title: Training inspiration

Training.noPaces: Add a best effort on your profile to see your personal paces.
Training.bikeNote: Bike workouts use heart-rate zones for now. Power targets come later.

easy-run.name: Easy run
easy-run.description: Relaxed, conversational pace. The base of all training.

long-run.name: Long run
long-run.description: Builds endurance. Keep it easy: time on your feet is what counts.

recovery-strides.name: Recovery run + strides
recovery-strides.description: Very easy running, then short, fast strides to stay sharp.

marathon-pace.name: Marathon-pace run
marathon-pace.description: A steady block at marathon pace. Comfortably hard.

progression-run.name: Progression run
progression-run.description: Start easy and finish at marathon pace.

long-run-mp.name: Long run with marathon blocks
long-run-mp.description: Marathon pace on tired legs: great for half and full marathon goals.

intervals-400.name: 12 × 400 m
intervals-400.description: Short, fast repeats for speed and running economy.

intervals-1k.name: 5 × 1 km
intervals-1k.description: Classic VO2max intervals. Hard but controlled.

cruise-intervals.name: Cruise intervals 4 × 8 min
cruise-intervals.description: Threshold running in blocks: raises the pace you can hold.

bike-endurance.name: Endurance ride
bike-endurance.description: Two hours in zone 2. Steady and relaxed.

bike-tempo.name: Tempo 3 × 12 min
bike-tempo.description: Long tempo efforts that build race-day strength.

bike-vo2.name: VO2max 5 × 4 min
bike-vo2.description: Hard efforts that raise your ceiling.

swim-technique.name: Technique swim

swim-aerobic.name: Aerobic 5 × 300 m
swim-aerobic.description: Steady, longer repeats that build swim endurance.

swim-threshold.name: Threshold 10 × 100 m
swim-threshold.description: Repeats at threshold pace, with a fast finish.

Goals.title: Goals
Goals.intro: Set a target based on your best efforts, and get simple tips on how to get there.

form.noBest: No best effort yet at this distance, so any target is fine.

errors.notFaster: You already did {time}. Pick a faster time.
errors.unavailable: Goals can't be saved right now. Please try again later.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

card.achieved: Goal reached! Time for a new one.
card.noBest: No best effort yet at this distance. Add one on your profile.

gap.close: Close. A few focused weeks can do it.
gap.season: Realistic in a season (8–16 weeks of steady training).
gap.big: A big step. Consider an in-between goal of {time}.

speed.slower: Your {reference} ({best}) is slower than that. Work on speed.
speed.supports: Your {reference} ({best}) already supports this goal. Focus on holding the pace for longer.
